children.text: The spacing select of the element toolbar

A small popover, as Claude Design has it, made of the design sidebar's own fields: the same combobox, so a value is typed or picked from the spacing scale the same way everywhere. Two fields per row, horizontal and vertical; the button at the end opens the row out to four sides.
The select shows the padding in pixels, in CSS order when the sides differ. Its popover drops from it.

Horizontal and vertical by default. The button opens a row to four fields, top and right, then bottom and left, as the sidebar lays them. When the sides of an axis already differ, the row opens with four.
The button's glyph is the icon of every field, with only the sides that field sets in white. Padding and margin share it; the row's title says which.
